summary: Shinko Mochizuki (1869–1948) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Tokuo Jobon, Togai Soga, and at Bukkyo University. He served as president of Shukyo University (1914–1928) and Taisho University (1930–1932), alongside other faculty roles.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under academic adviser Robert Bickner, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey.
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She held a professorship at Toyo University, attested in 2015.

Shinsho Hanayama (1898–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1918 to 1921. He taught Buddhism there from circa 1935 to 1959 and held posts at Toyo and Kokugakuin universities.

Shinshu Kusumoto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai (1912–1989) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held a post at Koyasan University, attested in 1959.

Shinya Moriyama (born 1972) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), and held a teaching post at Shinshu University around 2010.
Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1963 to 1967. He served as a professor at Otani University from circa 1995 to 2010.

Shiro Matsumoto (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi, and later served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1993–2016).

Shivaram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University and department head at Deccan College.

Shizuka Sasaki (born 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1989) under Jikido Takasaki, and served as professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from around 1992 to 2021.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University from around 1926 to 1927 and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from circa 1952 to 1977.
Shobha Rani Dash is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2010 and served as a lecturer at Otani University, attested in 2012.

Shodo Fujita (born 1959) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University, attested between 1995 and 2013.

Shodo Yamagami (born 1939) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1964 and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1974 to 2010.

Shogo Watanabe (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Toyo University (~1973–1983). He held faculty posts at Toyo University from around 1988 to 1995, and as professor from circa 1995 to 2019.

Shohaku Okumura (born 1948) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and trained under Kosho Uchiyama. He served at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center (1993–1996) and directed the Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (~1997–2003).

Shoji Mori (born 1938) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Giyu Nishi at Toyo University (~1962–1971). He served at Toyo University as assistant professor (~1977–1988) and professor (~1988–2009).

Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Otani University from around 1950 to 1981 and held a post as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
